proposal.reason: This uses the final experiment budget on a single controlled hyperparameter change grounded in exp-001's measured train-validation gap. All other XGBoost defaults and the full feature protocol remain unchanged.
proposal.hypothesis: Reducing scale_pos_weight from the automatic 12.248826291079812 to 1.5 while holding the full-input XGBoost configuration fixed will improve validation AUPRC by at least 0.005 by reducing overemphasis on positive-class gradients.
proposal.observation: The full-input default XGBoost improved validation AUPRC to 0.48298861837999635 from 0.18417067640399878, but train AUPRC is 0.7269248655343654 and the automatic scale_pos_weight is 12.248826291079812, indicating a substantial generalization gap under aggressive positive weighting.
proposal.expected_result: Validation AUPRC >= 0.4879886184. If it falls below this threshold, reject the lower class weight and retain exp-001.

previous_decision.reason: Exp-001 exceeded the predeclared improvement threshold and became the numeric validation incumbent at 0.48298861837999635.
previous_decision.learning: The bundled transition to full-input XGBoost produces a large validation-ranking gain over metadata-only logistic regression.
previous_decision.next_question: Can a less aggressive positive-class weight improve generalization while preserving the successful model and feature protocol?
